pages.title: Calculate one response
pages.text:
Calculate one response
For a patch with three identical rows (0, 0, 1),
Ax = 3 [(−1)(0)/3 + 0(0) + (1)(1)/3] = 1 .
Rows (1, 0, 0) give −1; a constant patch gives zero.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 5 / 19

pages.title: Count the valid window starts
pages.text:
Count the valid window starts
With size N , kernel width k, stride one and no padding,
Nout = N − k + 1.
16 − 3 + 1 = 14 .
Each output map is 14 × 14.

pages.title: Retain only positive responses
pages.text:
Retain only positive responses
Bxij = max(Axij, 0).
ReLU preserves positive rises and discards negative responses. For supplied intensities in
[0, 1], 0 ≤ Bxij ≤ 1.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 8 / 19

pages.title: An exact transpose check
pages.text:
An exact transpose check
The kernels satisfy Ky = KTx .
Transposing the image exchanges the pooled features:
f (I T ) = ( fy(I), fx(I)) .
A wide ellipse becomes tall relative to the axes.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 10 / 19

Fit the output rule
From training images only,
ck = 1nk ∑i:yi=k f (Ii).

pages.title: Weight sharing is not training
pages.text:
Weight sharing is not training
One 3 × 3 kernel has nine weights. They are reused at 196 locations.
Separate weights at
each location would require
196 · 9 = 1764
weights for one output map, before biases.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 12 / 19

pages.title: A learned convolution would update the kernels
pages.text:
A learned convolution would update the kernels
One possible extension has score
si = wT fK(Ii) + b
and loss 1n ∑i(si − yi)2.
Training would update selected parameters, including K. The
supplied ﬁlters remain ﬁxed.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 13 / 19

pages.title: An idealized contrast calculation
pages.text:
An idealized contrast calculation
Let I ′ = aI + b1, a ≥ 0, without clipping. Zero-sum ﬁlters give A(I ′) = aA(I).
ReLU
and averaging then give
f (I ′) = af (I).
The frozen class centers do not scale automatically.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 17 / 19

pages.title: An augmentation must respect the target
pages.text:
An augmentation must respect the target
A ninety-degree rotation swaps wide and tall relative to the axes.
Keeping the old label
would create a contradictory training example.
A contrast test preserves the intended orientation target while changing its visibility.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 18 / 19

pages.title: The fitted claim and its next test
pages.text:
The ﬁtted claim and its next test
The current claim concerns synthetic ellipse orientation and a ﬁxed observation process.
A new-patient claim requires patient separation, defensible labels and an appropriate
independent test.
More learned weights cannot replace those conditions.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 19 / 19
